title: High-Fidelity Inter-Species Rydberg Gates with Two-Photon Driving
abstract: Recently, neutral atom arrays have become known for their promising potential in quantum information processing. High-fidelity entangling operations are typically achieved by exciting atoms to high-lying Rydberg states through two-photon processes. To improve the performance of these systems at the hardware level, dual-species strategies have been applied to enhance readout, error correction, and reloading in neutral atom systems. However, the influence of laser crosstalk arising from two-photon excitation for dual-species systems has remained largely unexplored in the literature. Here, we develop a model that incorporates the influence of crosstalk in inter-species Rydberg gates with two-photon driving. We demonstrate that the influence of this crosstalk can be suppressed to arbitrarily small levels through appropriate gate design, with gate fidelities greater than $99.8\%$ achievable with conservative experimental parameters in the near-detuned case of an $^{85}$Rb/$^{87}$Rb system. We also outline how this fidelity can be further enhanced through improvements to the Rydberg excitation.
summary: This paper models high-fidelity entangling gates for dual-species neutral atom arrays using two-photon Rydberg excitation. It specifically addresses and mitigates the influence of laser crosstalk, a key challenge in scaling these quantum processors. The results show that fidelities exceeding 99.8% are achievable, paving the way for robust quantum information processing.
main_problem: The primary goal is to improve the fidelity of inter-species Rydberg gates in neutral atom arrays by modeling and suppressing the detrimental effects of laser crosstalk during two-photon driving.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that crosstalk can be suppressed to arbitrarily small levels, achieving gate fidelities greater than 99.8% using conservative parameters in an $^{85}	ext{Rb}/^{87}	ext{Rb}$ system.
method: The study develops a detailed model incorporating crosstalk into the Hamiltonian and uses time-optimal gate design principles to engineer the pulse sequence.
model_or_system: The system involves neutral atom arrays using dual-species isotopes ($^{85}	ext{Rb}/^{87}	ext{Rb}$) modeled as five-level systems. The dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating the full Hamiltonian, including van der Waals interactions and laser driving fields.
key_observables: Gate fidelity (target $>99.8\%$), unitary infidelity, and full infidelity including decoherence.
important_parameters: Near-detuned regime, specific parameters for $^{85}	ext{Rb}$ and $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ (listed in Table I), and the gate time ($T$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes global and overlapping laser fields, and the gate design is optimized using time-optimal gate approaches.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level diagrams, the evolution of infidelity vs. time (comparing unitary vs. full), and the required phase modulations for the gate operation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical system and the problem of crosstalk, develops the comprehensive model and Hamiltonian, details the time-optimal gate design, presents the results showing high fidelity, and concludes by outlining future enhancement possibilities.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles a critical hardware-level limitation (crosstalk) in a leading platform for quantum computation (neutral atoms), providing concrete, high-fidelity gate protocols.
